title: As Driven convention rule registry
description: Rules describing how cars of a given mechanism and era were usually driven, for display where the real car's value is unknown. A rule never supplies a value to a record and is never an authentic claim: it is evidence about a class, shown as convention rather than as a finding about the car. See docs/convention-guidance.md.

when.description: The antecedent. Every stated condition must match the record's own established values for the rule to apply. A condition naming 'unknown' matches a record that has not established that field.

then.description: The fields this rule speaks to. A rule only ever describes a field the record leaves unknown; it never overrides, contradicts or outranks an established value.

strength.description: How reliably the class behaved this way. Inversely related to how much the era varied: near-certain where practice was effectively universal, usual where exceptions are known and documented.

guidance.description: The sentence a driver reads where there is room for it. It must say that the real car's value is not established before saying what such cars usually did.

short_guidance.description: The same sentence for a client with one line to spend, such as the overlay card. It carries the same hedge and the same instruction; the reasoning it drops lives in `guidance` and in the catalog. This bound is a coarse guard - the binding one is width, which the client tests measure against the narrowest card the plugin draws.
